transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-08-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Pegasus CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Pegasus ML Eng), Daniel Park (Pegasus SRE)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough on quantization profiles (INT8/FP8). Showed perf/quality tradeoffs, sample benchmarks on conversational prompts, discussed POC scope and security/compliance needs.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Liam, our systems engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:07 - Rajiv Menon: Good, thanks. Excited to dig in — we had some questions around INT8 vs FP8 and whether the quality loss is acceptable for our customer-facing chat flows.
00:16 - Sofia Alvarez: Yep, and latency is super important for us, we have 95th percentile goals under 350ms for short replies but also a lot of long context 4k token prompts for summarization.
00:27 - Liam O'Connor: Great, that's exactly what we'll talk through — we'll show how Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles and tradeoffs. Quick agenda: walk through the profiles, show our sample benchmark numbers, then discuss POC scope and security. Sound good?
00:42 - Daniel Park: Yep, good. Also curious about host vs dedicated costs — if we go INT8 on shared hosted, will we hit any noisy neighbor or stability issues?
00:51 - Maya Chen: Good point. We'll cover routing, dedicated capacity options and fallback policies.

02:15 - Liam O'Connor: Alright, starting with quantization basics — INT8 reduces memory and compute by using 8-bit integers; it's been solid for many causal and chat models but you can see some lexical errors or slight factuality drops in very sensitive tasks. FP8 is newer, keeps more floating precision and often closer to FP16 quality while still cutting memory vs FP16. In practice FP8 tends to give much of the speed benefit with smaller quality delta than INT8 on some models.

03:30 - Sofia Alvarez: Is FP8 supported across all the open models? We mainly use a Llama-family variant and a retrieval-augmented transformer for summarization.
03:40 - Liam O'Connor: Support depends on the backend kernels; Redwood's optimize engine recommends per-model profiles. For Llama-family we have INT8-Tuned and FP8 profiles; FP8 usually preserves generation coherence better for long-context tasks like your 4k prompts.

05:05 - Rajiv Menon: Can you quantify "preserves coherence" — like what's the delta we should expect on Rouge/BLEU or a human eval?
05:13 - Liam O'Connor: Good question. On our internal benchmarks for a 4k summarization set, INT8 showed an average quality drop of ~1.8 to 3.5% on ROUGE-L versus FP16 baseline, whereas FP8 was ~0.4 to 1.1% drop. Latency wise, INT8 gives ~25-35% lower token p99 on same hardware; FP8 gives ~15-25%. Numbers vary by model and prompt distribution.

07:02 - Sofia Alvarez: So for chat/short replies where latency matters most, INT8 might make sense. For long summarization jobs we should probably pick FP8?
07:12 - Liam O'Connor: Exactly. Another lever is dynamic profile routing: route short low-risk traffic to INT8 for cost/latency and high-importance long-context to FP8 or FP16. Redwood supports per-route policies and automatic fallback if quality-regression thresholds are triggered.

09:30 - Daniel Park: On the dedicated vs hosted question — if we reserve dedicated GPUs can we lock in a profile or will Redwood still apply optimize suggestions?
09:40 - Maya Chen: You can pin model versions and baseline profiles on Dedicated. Optimize will still provide recommendations and you can opt into automated rollouts. For strict production SLAs customers often pin a conservative profile and run Optimize in advisory mode.

11:05 - Rajiv Menon: For our security/compliance team — we need audit logs, KMS integration, and clear data residency controls. Are these supported for POC?
11:14 - Maya Chen: Yes, Private and Dedicated support KMS/HSM and VPC options. We can share the SOC 2 docs and architecture diagrams after the call. I'll add those to next steps.

12:50 - Liam O'Connor: Showing the sample benchmark sheet now — (link shared) — these are synthetic runs on a 4x A100-ish cluster, sample prompts were a mix of 512–4k tokens. Note: transcription: that link might render oddly in the transcript, but you'll get the spreadsheet.

14:00 - Liam O'Connor: For the conversational bucket (avg 120 tokens), INT8 gave 45% cost reduction per token and p95 latency dropped from 220ms to 140ms. For 4k summarization, FP8 kept ROUGE within 1% of FP16 while reducing memory by ~40% — enabling larger batch sizes and better throughput.

16:30 - Sofia Alvarez: How do caching and KV cache affect these numbers? Our RAG pipeline uses a lot of prefix caching.
16:40 - Liam O'Connor: Good point. KV/prefix cache cuts the token generation path for repeated context; that amplifies latency gains from quantization because you reduce compute for the decoding steps. Batching parameters also interact: larger batches increase throughput but can hurt p95 latency — Redwood Optimize recommends profile-specific batching settings.

18:10 - Rajiv Menon: Any gotchas for hallucinations when moving to INT8? We've had customers complain about subtle factual errors.
18:20 - Liam O'Connor: INT8 can slightly affect logits precision, occasionally changing rare-token probabilities; that can surface as hallucination for prompt-sensitive tasks. Mitigations: temperature tuning, reranking, or running a secondary FP8/FP16 verification step for high-risk outputs. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions via evals and auto-fallback to a safer profile for flagged routes.

21:05 - Daniel Park: Cost modeling — if we estimate 2M tokens/month in prod, ballpark cost difference between hosted INT8 vs hosted FP8 vs Dedicated?
21:18 - Maya Chen: I'll send a detailed spreadsheet but ballpark: hosted INT8 often saves 30–40% vs hosted FP16; FP8 sits in the middle ~15–25% savings. Dedicated committed capacity lowers unit cost substantially — plus predictable throughput — we'll put numbers in the follow-up.

24:00 - Sofia Alvarez: For the POC, we'd want a set of 100 golden prompts for summarization and 200 chat traces to run evals. Can Redwood run those or do we upload?
24:12 - Liam O'Connor: For POC we generally ask customers to provide representative prompt sets; we can also run our suite if you prefer. We recommend parity tests: run on FP16 baseline, INT8, FP8 and then compute quality metrics + latency profiles.

27:40 - Rajiv Menon: Timeline wise — if we start POC next week, how long to show meaningful results?
27:48 - Maya Chen: Typical short POCs are 2–3 weeks to run benchmarks, a week to review, then iterate. If you want deep integration (VPC, KMS) that adds time for networking and security review — usually 3–5 weeks.

30:05 - Daniel Park: Network egress and audit logs — will using hosted cause any data to hit Redwood systems unsecured? Our security folks want to be clear.
30:15 - Maya Chen: Hosted encrypts in transit and at rest, we support customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private; we'll share the SOC 2 and architecture diagrams in the follow-up. For highly sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private.

32:50 - Liam O'Connor: Quick demo clip: showing Optimize console where you can compare profiles side-by-side — quality delta column, latency P50/P95, and recommended batching. (Screen share/brief pause).

35:10 - Sofia Alvarez: The UI looks helpful — can we create a canary route to test INT8 on 10% of traffic?
35:18 - Liam O'Connor: Yes, the rollout tooling supports canary percentages, auto rollback on eval regressions, and route-level policies.

37:35 - Rajiv Menon: Competitor question — we've seen some claims from Aurora Inference about near-FP16 accuracy on INT8, is that comparable?
37:45 - Liam O'Connor: Different stacks optimize differently; some kernel-level optimizations can narrow gaps. Redwood focuses on per-model profiles + eval-driven rollouts rather than a one-size-fits-all claim. We'll share comparative notes on Triton and others in the doc bundle.

40:00 - Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps: Maya will send benchmark spreadsheet, pricing, SOC 2 and architecture diagrams; Liam will run sample perf tests on Pegasus prompts; Rajiv will share retention/compliance requirements; we'll schedule a POC scoping session next week.

41:12 - Rajiv Menon: Sounds good, please also include a short runbook for how we toggle profiles during canary.
41:20 - Liam O'Connor: Will do — short doc with CLI/API steps and recommended thresholds.

43:00 - Sofia Alvarez: One more minor question — do you throttle or rate-limit differently by profile?
43:06 - Maya Chen: Rate limits are per-route and you can set profile-specific quotas. We'll include sample configs.

45:10 - Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items discussed.
45:15 - Daniel Park: Thanks, bye.
45:18 - Rajiv Menon: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and proper nouns sometimes mis-attributed; some metric numbers are rounded for conversational clarity.
